title: L. Annaeus Seneca on Benefits
author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
public_title: Your hustle isn’t the key to health
hook: You think you need constant hustle to stay healthy.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You think you need constant hustle to stay healthy. Yet Seneca wrote that true wellbeing comes from giving benefits to others, not endless effort. The result? Your brain lights up when you help. Modern science backs him up. A 2008 study by Elizabeth Dunn at the University of British Columbia, Canada, found that spending money on others raised happiness. The increase was about 15 % compared to self‑spending. Not just one group—later research in 2015 by the University of Chicago’s Center for Health and Happiness, Chicago, showed regular volunteers reported about 20 % lower depression rates. This pattern is called the altruism‑wellbeing link. Studies also show that kindness improves immune function. So why do we assume selfish grind equals health? Because culture glorifies busywork, not generosity. The fact is generosity triggers dopamine and reduces stress hormones. So next time you feel pressured to grind, remember giving back actually fuels your health. That's it. You think you need constant hustle to stay healthy.
